items.text: The system shall support discovery of local businesses or services using a searchable query and a geographic location.

claims.claim: The main page provides a local business search form with a service or business query field and a geographic location field.
The user can set a business or service query and a geographic location together in the search form.

items.evidence_note: The UI shows a two-field search form and the entered query 'hair salon' with San Diego location context.
items.rationale: All visible core claims for searchable local discovery are supported by the search form and entered search context.

items.text: The system shall provide query autocomplete or quick-result suggestions while the user types a business or service term.

claims.claim: When the user types a business or service term, the interface displays query suggestions or quick results related to that term.

items.evidence_note: After 'hair salon' is entered, a quick-results panel appears with related suggestions.
items.rationale: The autocomplete or quick-result behavior is directly visible while the query field contains the typed service term.

items.text: The system shall provide location autocomplete or quick-location suggestions while the user edits the location field.

claims.claim: When the user edits the location field, the interface displays quick-location suggestions matching the typed location text.

items.evidence_note: The location field shows San Diego input and a quick-location dropdown with multiple San Diego-related places.
items.rationale: The visible dropdown directly supports location autocomplete or quick-location suggestions.

items.text: The system shall resolve a typed location into a more specific canonical place label for search context.

claims.claim: A typed location can be represented as a more specific canonical place label.

items.evidence_note: The location field changes from 'San Diego' to 'San Diego, CA'.
items.rationale: The visible search context shows a more specific location label after location editing.

items.text: The system shall provide an explicit action to submit the current search criteria once the user has set the desired query and location.

claims.claim: After the query and location are set, the interface provides an explicit search submission control.

items.evidence_note: The 'Find' button is visible next to the filled query and location fields.
items.rationale: The visible 'Find' action satisfies the requirement for an explicit search submission mechanism.

items.text: The system shall provide signed-in users with access to account-level sections such as favorites, coupons, profile, and settings.

claims.claim: The interface shows a signed-in account area for the current user.
The signed-in account area provides access entries for favorites, coupons, profile, and settings.

items.evidence_note: The right-side account panel says 'Hi James S.' and lists Favorites, Coupons, Profile, and Settings.
items.rationale: The visible signed-in menu provides the requested account-level sections.

items.text: The system shall expose coupons as a user-facing discovery feature within the service.

claims.claim: The interface exposes a user-facing Coupons entry point.
The system exposes coupon discovery content or coupon results inside the service.

items.evidence_note: A Coupons entry is visible in the signed-in account panel, but no coupon listing or coupon discovery page is shown.
items.rationale: The visible entry point supports the feature exposure, while the actual discovery content is not visible in this screenshot flow.

items.text: The system shall allow users to pursue coupon discovery for a searched business category within a chosen locality.
items.annotation_notes: The task goal is coupon-oriented, the UI exposes a coupons section, and the flow configures a localized hair salon search. Together these cues support a plausible requirement that coupons can be sought in relation to a selected business category and place, even though the final coupon page is not shown.

claims.claim: The system supports a business category search context configured with a chosen locality.
The interface exposes coupons as a possible user-facing area.
The system provides coupon discovery results or a coupon path for the selected category and locality.

items.evidence_note: The flow configures 'hair salon' with 'San Diego, CA' and shows a Coupons entry, but it does not show coupon results for that search.
items.rationale: The visible setup and coupon entry support part of the requirement, but the category-and-locality-specific coupon discovery outcome is not shown.

items.text: The system shall assist geographic disambiguation by presenting multiple matching locations, including city and neighborhood-level options, when a location is ambiguous.

claims.claim: When location input is ambiguous, the system presents multiple matching location options.
The location suggestions include both city-level and neighborhood or area-level options.

items.evidence_note: The dropdown includes city-level entries such as San Diego, CA and San Diego, TX, plus area entries such as Mission Hills, Serra Mesa, Downtown, and other San Diego neighborhoods.
items.rationale: The visible quick-location list supports geographic disambiguation with multiple city and neighborhood-level options.

items.text: The system shall provide alternative category entry points for common local-business searches from the main discovery page.
items.annotation_notes: The homepage shows shortcuts such as Find People, Restaurants, Auto Repair, Dentists, Veterinarians, and Attorneys, indicating support for multiple category-based discovery paths from the same entry point.
items.manual_verification_notes: UI after pressing a alternative route is missing

claims.claim: The main discovery page provides category shortcuts for common local-business searches.

items.evidence_note: The page shows shortcuts such as Find People, Restaurants, Auto Repair, Dentists, Veterinarians, and Attorneys.
items.rationale: The visible category shortcuts provide alternative entry points from the main page.

items.text: The system shall provide a unified search workflow in which the user can set both service type and location before launching a search.

claims.claim: Users can set both service type and location before launching a search.
The system provides a search launch action after service type and location are set.

items.evidence_note: Steps 2 to 4 show the service type and location being set in the same search workflow, with a Find action still present.
items.rationale: The flow supports setting both criteria before launching the search.

items.text: The system shall support searching for service categories such as hair salons within a selected city.
items.annotation_notes: Search configuration and launch mechanism are supported, while the returned-results outcome is not covered.

claims.claim: The system supports searching for service categories such as hair salons within a selected city.

items.evidence_note: The flow configures a hair salon search in San Diego, CA and shows the Find action, but no result page is shown after submission.
items.rationale: Search configuration and launch mechanism are supported, while the returned-results outcome is not covered.

items.text: The system shall maintain consistency of user-entered search context across sequential edits so that the chosen query and location remain visible together before submission.

claims.claim: The chosen query is maintained across sequential search-context edits.
The chosen query and location remain visible together before submission.

items.evidence_note: The hair salon query remains present while the location is edited, and step 4 shows hair salon with San Diego, CA together before search submission.
items.rationale: The visible form state preserves the search context across sequential edits.

items.text: The system shall allow signed-in users to save coupon discoveries to favorites and revisit them from account-level areas in later use.

claims.claim: Account-level areas for favorites and coupons are available to signed-in users.
Signed-in users can save coupon discoveries to favorites.
Saved coupon discoveries can be revisited from account-level areas in later use.

items.evidence_note: Favorites and Coupons are visible in the account area, but no coupon discovery, save action, saved coupon, or later revisit state is shown.
items.rationale: The relevant account areas are visible, while saving and later-use persistence are not verified.

items.text: The system shall let users open a discovered coupon into a redeemable detail or outbound handoff that provides merchant-facing usage instructions.

claims.claim: Coupon-related functionality is exposed as service context.
Users can open a discovered coupon.
An opened coupon provides redeemable detail or outbound handoff.
The redeemable detail or outbound handoff provides merchant-facing usage instructions.

items.evidence_note: The flow shows only a Coupons entry. It does not show a discovered coupon, an opened coupon, redemption details, merchant-facing instructions, or an outbound handoff.
items.rationale: The screenshots do not contain the coupon discovery state needed to evaluate this requirement reliably.

items.text: The system shall surface only currently valid coupon offers that match the active business category and resolved locality.

claims.claim: An active business category and resolved locality are available as search context.
The system surfaces coupon offers for the active business category and resolved locality.
Only currently valid coupon offers are surfaced.
Only coupon offers matching the active business category and resolved locality are surfaced.

items.evidence_note: The search context is visible, but no coupon offers are shown. Offer validity and match correctness cannot be verified from the screenshots.
items.rationale: The core coupon-offer behavior is not present in the flow, so a reliable positive or negative verdict is not possible.

items.text: The system shall present complete geographic disambiguation coverage for ambiguous location input, including all relevant city and neighborhood matches before the user commits the search.

claims.claim: The system presents city-level matches for ambiguous location input before search commitment.
The system presents neighborhood-level matches for ambiguous location input before search commitment.
The geographic disambiguation coverage includes all relevant city and neighborhood matches.

items.evidence_note: The flow shows many San Diego-related city and neighborhood or area suggestions, but completeness over all relevant matches cannot be established from screenshots alone.
items.rationale: The visible disambiguation behavior is supported, while the strengthened completeness obligation is not fully verifiable.

items.text: The system shall present a dedicated coupon results or review step after search submission that summarizes matching offers for the selected business category and locality.

claims.claim: The selected business category and locality are available before submission.
Search submission occurs after the selected business category and locality are set.
A dedicated coupon results or review step is presented after search submission.
The coupon results or review step summarizes matching offers for the selected business category and locality.

items.evidence_note: Step 4 shows the configured search context, but the flow does not show the search being submitted or any later coupon results or review step.
items.rationale: Missing a post-submission state is not visible counter-evidence, so the safest label is abstain.

items.text: The system shall carry the resolved canonical location label and active search term forward onto later coupon discovery views so users can confirm or revise the current search context.

claims.claim: The active search term and resolved canonical location label are available together before submission.
The resolved canonical location label and active search term are carried forward onto later coupon discovery views.
Users can confirm the current search context on later coupon discovery views.
Users can revise the current search context on later coupon discovery views.

items.evidence_note: The active search term and resolved location are visible before submission, but the flow contains no later coupon discovery view.
items.rationale: There is not enough visible evidence to judge whether the context is carried forward or revisable later.
